summary: A symmetrical structure featuring a central tiered building surrounded by four tall, square corner towers. The walls are characterized by distinct horizontal bands of contrasting materials, and the roofs are predominantly made of stone slabs with red brick accents. The building sits within a rectangular perimeter marked by spaced white blocks.

shape.overall_form: Central tiered mass with four detached or semi-detached corner towers

materials.name: brick
materials.role: roof accents and tower roof bases

rebuild_hints: Lay out the rectangular footprint using the white block perimeter as a guide.
Erect the four corner towers using dark stone pillars on the edges and sandstone walls in between, leaving 1-block gaps for glass windows.
Build the central structure's walls using alternating horizontal bands of sandstone, wood planks, and white blocks.
Construct the central tiered roof using stone slabs, stepping inwards and upwards, and add brick accents along the tier transitions.
Top each of the four towers with a flat, overhanging roof made of stone slabs and bricks, and place a light-emitting block at the very center top.
uncertainties: Interior layout and materials are completely unknown as there are no visible entrances or interior views.
Exact block dimensions are estimated from exterior visual proportions.
Specific variants of wood (e.g., oak vs. birch) and dark stone (e.g., deepslate vs. dark stone brick) are difficult to determine with absolute certainty.
